Walmart just told us who's winning the affordability fight — and it's Walmart.

In its earnings today, the retailer said U.S. online sales grew about 23% last quarter and raised its full-year outlook for the third time this year (Walmart Q3, Nov. 19).

Why? Shoppers are trading down. When groceries, rent and card bills bite, even higher-income families head to the discounter to stretch a dollar — so Walmart's growth is really a map of who's feeling squeezed.

It's the same pressure in Canada, where inflation is stuck at 3.1% and grocery prices are rising faster (Statistics Canada, October).

My take: a store booming because everyone's pinching pennies isn't a feel-good story — it's the squeeze, wearing a smiley face.

Where are you cutting back first when money's tight — groceries, going out, or subscriptions?
